title: Reading Data: Averages, Spread, and Relationships

questions.question: The number of goals scored in a match is what type of data?
questions.rationale: Goals are countable whole numbers, so the data are discrete quantitative — unlike continuous data such as height or time, which are measured.

questions.question: In the frequency table (4 marks ×3, 6 marks ×5, 8 marks ×8, 10 marks ×4), what is the mean?
Which average is most appropriate for reporting household incomes in a city?
questions.rationale: A few very large incomes drag the mean upward, while the median — a positional average — barely moves. This robustness is why median income is reported.

questions.question: One billionaire joins a village of 100 farmers. Which average changes the most?
questions.rationale: The mean counts size, so one huge value drags it far above what anyone earns; the median counts only position and moves by about one place.

questions.question: For the data 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 12: Q1 = 5 and Q3 = 10. What is the IQR?
questions.rationale: IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 10 − 5 = 5, the width of the middle half of the data. (9 is the range, 12 − 3.)

questions.question: Datasets A and B both have mean 6, but SD(A) ≈ 1.41 and SD(B) ≈ 3.69. What does this tell you?
options: B's values cluster more tightly around 6
B's values are more spread out around 6
questions.rationale: Standard deviation measures spread around the mean: same centre, but B's values deviate much more — standard deviation detects differences the mean cannot.

questions.question: In a pie chart of 30 students' transport choices, 12 students walk. What angle should the 'walk' sector have?
questions.rationale: The pie angle equals the fraction of the total times 360°: 12/30 × 360° = 144°. All sector angles must total 360°.

questions.question: What is the key difference between a bar chart and a histogram?
options: Histograms use colors, bar charts do not
Bar charts suit continuous data with touching bars; histograms suit discrete categories
Bar charts suit discrete categories with gaps; histograms suit continuous classes with no gaps
questions.rationale: Bar charts display discrete categories separated by gaps; histograms display continuous class intervals with no gaps, and area carries frequency.

questions.question: Ice-cream sales and drowning incidents rise together every summer. What is the correct interpretation?
options: Hot weather likely drives both — a confounding variable
questions.rationale: Correlation is not causation: a confounding variable (hot weather) can raise both quantities without either causing the other. Only controlled experiments establish causation.

questions.question: Hours of practice and typing errors move in opposite directions. This is an example of:
questions.rationale: When one variable rises while the other falls, the scatter plot shows negative correlation — practice hours up, errors down.
